Jocelyn Palm, for the past several years Executive 
Secretary of the Ontario Branch of the Royal Life Sav 
Society, has received the promotion, one richly deserved, to the 
Canadian National Branch as Associate Executive Director. This means 
that, through close association and travel, Jocelyn will provide opportunities for 
the National Office to assist each province. Take a tip from us. .. Jocelyn is a great 
gal to know and if you have a question concerning any aspect of camping, ask her. She’ll 
have the answer for you and, if not, she’ll get it for you! We know because she is a valued member 
of the Editorial Committee and, in this capacity, she has promised to be our liaison across Canada so, if 
you receive a phone call from her, don’t be surprised! Congratulations and all the best in your new venture, Joe! 

One of the key speakers at the fall gathering of the Society of Camp Directors was John Walker of Cornwall, Ontario, 
now studying for a Master’s Degree at York University. He was the recipient of the first Research Award of the Society and 



he based his report on his findings and 
conclusions regarding the matter of 
professionalism and the training of 
Camp Directors. We hear that the 
B.C.C.A. continues to thrive as a strong 
dynamic Association . .. due in part to 
people like Rick Ryan, Dave Campbell 
and Ken Goodwin . . . and, of course, 
the people in camping on the west 
coast always know they can count on 
May Brown for her continued interest 
and support.We wonder if you 
know that, at the time of Tanya Kris- 
man’s tragic death, the B.C.C.A. dedi¬ 
cated a memorial to Tanya. Money 
donations were requested with the 
proviso that something in Tanya’s 
memory at the new site for Camp 
YaWaCa on Salt Spring Island would 
be established. We understand that the 
renovation of the farmhouse, “Skip¬ 
per’s Shack”, cost $5,000. Tanya’s 
daughter, Pat, chose the farmhouse to 
be named for her because they had 
stayed there during building operations 
and had had such happy times. The 
fund is not going well and Camp 
YaWaCa needs the help of camping 
folk across Canada. Tanya did so much 
for the C.C.A. and was one of its 
keenest supporters. Now it’s time for 
all of us in C.C.A. to support some¬ 
thing that Tanya believed whole¬ 
heartedly in . . . Camp YaWaCa. 

A big tip of the hat to Alberta! And 
why? Because of its enthusiastic re¬ 
sponse, spear-headed by the efforts of 
its President, Jan James, to our request 
for articles. Our readers will be the 
richer because they’re excellent and 
will be in forthcoming issues. You 
might be interested to know that for 


this Winter Edition, we have one article 
from B.C., one from Manitoba and the 
rest are from Ontario. Isn’t it time to 
make this magazine a true Canadian 
one? We think so. But how? YOU 
have the answer.^* Hank Roessingh 
is very involved in and excited about 
his new position as the Applications 
Editor for the Canadian Arctic Gas 
Study, a group of 25 companies, in¬ 
cluding the CPR, CNR, Can. Develop¬ 
ment Corp’n, Trans-Canada Pipeline, 
Alberta Gas Trunk and also a number 
of American gas pipeline companies, 
who will, sometime in 1973, ask the 
Canadian Government, through the 
Dept, of Indian and Northern Affairs, 
the National Energy Board, etc., for 
permission to build a gas pipeline from 
Alaska via Canada to Alberta and on 
to Ontario and the Chicago area. Hank 
states that the precautions against pol¬ 
lution and disturbing the environment, 
that they have to take, are almost 
incredible. Tim Easley, in the Dept, 

of Forestry at the Univ. of Fredericton, 
was recently elected President of the 
N.B.C.A. with Dave Goss as Vice- 
President. Rick Gilbert and Debbie 

Rose of the Halifax Y.M.C.A. are two 
new “lights” on the camping scene in 
Nova Scotia and will be helping the 
President,David Boston.'-*' 0 Tony Fry, 
Chairman of the OCA Conference, has 
been appointed Director of Camping 
Services for the Toronto Y.M.C.A. 
We’re sure you’ll be interested in a few 
items about the OCA Conference to be 
held at the Sheraton Four Seasons 
Hotel in downtown Toronto, March 
8th to 10th. The excitement of being 
in entirely new surroundings will be 


nothing compared to the programme 
being offered to camp directors and 
senior personnel. A catch phrase to 
express it all would be “Don’t tell us! 
Show us!” In the past few years, the 
style of the OCA Conference has been 
that of using a session speaker to 
present a topic that would lead into a 
general discussion with those in atten¬ 
dance. The evaluations told us this 
often .resulted in the sharing of ignor¬ 
ance or a certain few monopolizing the 
conversation. BUT not this year... we 
will listen and leave with something 
new and vital because experts on the 
topic are going to tell us about kitchen 
organization and ideas, selection and 
interviewing of staff, promotion and 
public relations, drama, Indian Lore, 
staff training, adventure camping, in¬ 
teresting the older camper, canoe trip¬ 
ping, the camper today, the waterfront, 
outdoor cookery, 10 sure-fire campfire 
stunts, aids to sailors and much more. 
In addition, there will be practical 
demonstrations concerning the making 
of paddles and looms, waterfront 
structuring, archery, arts and crafts, 
orienteering and pottery. And still 
more . . . something new is to be 
offered in the Media Room. You will 
have an opportunity to view copying 
equipment and a Cassette tape recorder 
which you can use to record, for your 
own personal files, contracts, singsongs, 
programme ideas, a ten day menu, etc., 
which will be on display. Sounds very 
intriguing and exciting, doesn’t it? 
Why not circle the date, March 8th- 
10th, on your calendar and plan to 
join us at the Four Seasons. Seems 
like a great idea to us. A
